newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns first ratings to Latvia.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns first ratings to Latvia.

text.p: Former Soviet republic Latvia received its ratings from Standard & Poor's with the U.S. credit rating agency assigning a BBB rating to its long-term foreign currency debt.
S&P assigned an A- rating to Latvia's long term local currency debt and an A-3 short term foreign currency and A-2 short term local currency rating.
"The outlook on the long-term debt ratings is stable," S&P said in a statement.

"Accelerated restructuring through the privatisation of most large enterprises over the next year, together with conservative fiscal and monetary policies, should lead to faster rates of growth over the remainder of the decade."

S&P said the current ratings also reflect the expectation that if privatisation falters or banking sector pressures reemerge, prudent management, plus the buffer provided by very low debt levels, should contain negative economic impact and ensure the slippage is only temporary.
The agency said the ratings reflected the country's success in instituting market-based economic reforms and the government's ongoing commitment to the reform process.
It also reflected the flexibility afforded by the country's low fiscal debt and net external liability and broad support for continued prudent fiscal and monetary management.

But on the other hand, the ratings were constrained by low, albeit rising income levels, the uncertain competitive position of the yet-to-be-privatised large enterprises, and possible inflationary pressures arising from the need for further upwards adjustments in hosuing, ulitity and fuel prices.
